question.text: A portfolio manager holding a diversified equity portfolio worth Rs. 50 crore believes the market will fall 10% in the next month. To hedge, she sells NIFTY futures covering the portfolio's market exposure. If the market falls 10% as forecast, what is the net outcome (ignoring basis risk and fees)?

answer.text: Rs. 5 crore gain on futures and Rs. 5 crore loss on portfolio = near zero net change
Rs. 5 crore loss on both — net Rs. 10 crore loss
Rs. 5 crore gain on portfolio, nothing from futures
Rs. 10 crore gain on futures, Rs. 5 crore loss on portfolio

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook states that a manager can sell index futures to protect a diversified equity portfolio. If the market falls 10%, the portfolio declines by about Rs. 5 crore and the sold Nifty futures gain about Rs. 5 crore, so the hedged position is roughly flat. The Trap: The other options miss the hedging mechanic — a short futures position gains when the market drops, so neither a double loss nor a one-sided gain is consistent with selling futures against a long portfolio. Note: Portfolio managers may use derivatives per the PMS agreement, including for hedging and portfolio rebalancing, subject to the required disclosures and controls. The workbook also references tactical allocation and alpha uses within the same framework.
